headline: High data-leakage and capability-conflict risk: aci can reach CRM/email/Slack while the course agent writes locally and handles secrets, creating unsafe cross-agent data flow by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can ingest and emit content through email, Slack, Notion, Sheets, CRM, and MCP-style tool use, while the course agent reads/writes local files and runs shell commands. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if aci content is copied into the course agent or shared via files. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF aci outputs untrusted text into a file or message that the course agent later parses as instructions, injection is possible.
IF the two agents share a workspace or copy-paste bridge, attacker-controlled content can cross from aci to the course agent.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct workspaces.
Require a human review step before the course agent consumes aci output.
Strip instructions from copied text and keep only structured fields.
Disable automatic file ingestion from shared folders.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, support, and research data and has broad network egress; the course agent reads/writes files and handles configuration secrets. If they share files or a workspace, sensitive data can move from aci into the course agent and then out through its shell/network tooling. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default local-dev setups, so this is high.
conditions: IF aci exports CRM/email/support data into files accessible to the course agent, leakage can occur.
IF the course agent is given access to the same directory as aci outputs, secrets or customer data can be read and forwarded.
mitigations: Keep aci outputs in a separate directory with restrictive permissions.
Do not mount the same workspace into both agents.
Redact secrets before passing any files to the course agent.
Review outbound destinations for both agents before enabling them.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation and DLP scanning.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and broad API-based actions, while the course agent can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and write files. Even though modify_git_state is false, overlapping mutable surfaces still exist through files and external services. Without stated locking or coordination, concurrent runs can overwrite each other’s artifacts or credentials.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or shared external service, their updates can race.
IF aci and the course agent operate on the same CRM-like or file-backed artifact without locks, one can overwrite the other.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Avoid concurrent runs against the same external resource.
Check for existing artifacts before writing.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control to shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar content and the course agent exposes agentic ask/stream endpoints plus shell/file actions. If the course agent treats aci output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or published content. There is no documented verification step between them, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF the course agent consumes aci-generated text without validation, it may propagate hallucinations or stale CRM facts.
IF aci output is used to draft files or commands, downstream actions can be based on incorrect assumptions.
mitigations: Require a verification step before acting on aci output.
Use schema validation for any structured handoff.
Limit the course agent to drafting, not executing, on first pass.
Log source provenance alongside each handoff.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking against source systems.

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles CRM, email, support, and calendar data, while the course agent handles configuration secrets and runs in a local development environment with Docker/Airflow credentials. If regulated customer data from aci is moved into the course agent’s environment, retention and access controls can diverge. The profiles do not state matching compliance controls, so the mismatch is a medium-risk compliance gap.
conditions: IF customer or support data from aci is copied into the course agent environment, retention and access policies may diverge.
IF the course agent logs or stores those inputs, compliance obligations can be violated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the course agent environment.
Review retention settings for logs and notebooks.
Use synthetic or anonymized data for testing.
Restrict access to Docker and Airflow credentials.
requires-engineering: document and enforce a shared data-handling policy.
